check.question: Return up to three team IDs and their positive backlog counts at the end of March 31, 2026, ordered by count descending and then team ID ascending.
check.sql:
WITH cutoff AS (SELECT '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AS cutoff_at),
ticket_state AS (
  SELECT t.ticket_id,
         (SELECT se.to_status
            FROM ticket_events e
            JOIN ticket_status_events se ON se.event_id = e.event_id
           WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
             AND e.occurred_at < (SELECT cutoff_at FROM cutoff)
           ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.seq DESC
           LIMIT 1) AS status,
         (SELECT ae.to_team_id
            FROM ticket_events e
            JOIN ticket_assignment_events ae ON ae.event_id = e.event_id
           WHERE e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
             AND e.occurred_at < (SELECT cutoff_at FROM cutoff)
           ORDER BY e.occurred_at DESC, e.seq DESC
           LIMIT 1) AS team_id
    FROM tickets t
   WHERE t.created_at < (SELECT cutoff_at FROM cutoff)
)
SELECT ts.team_id, COUNT(*) AS backlog_count
  FROM ticket_state ts
 WHERE ts.status IN (SELECT status_code FROM ticket_statuses WHERE counts_as_backlog = 1)
 GROUP BY ts.team_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
 ORDER BY backlog_count DESC, ts.team_id ASC
 LIMIT 3;

check.witness: Teams 30 and 40 both end the March cutoff with exactly 4 backlog tickets (team 30: tickets 12-15; team 40: tickets 16-19). The brief breaks the 4-4 tie by team ID ascending, so the third row is (30, 4); the wrong query only reverses the tie-break (ORDER BY backlog_count DESC, ts.team_id DESC) and returns (40, 4) instead. Note ticket 1 is pending (not open) at the cutoff, ticket 3 reopens twice on 2026-03-10 (seq 3 open, seq 4 closed, seq 5 open) and is counted once under team 10, and the 2026-04-01 00:00:00 events (ticket 1 close, ticket 2 transfer to team 50 and close/reopen) are excluded by the exclusive cutoff, leaving team 50 with zero backlog and out of the positive-only result.
